syllabus_topics: Real numbers: algebraic, order, and supremum axioms
Sequences: the concept of limit; applications
Real functions of a real variable; limits and continuity; elementary functions
Global properties of continuous functions: intermediate value and Weierstrass theorems
Antidifferentiation: by parts, substitution, rational functions

Applications: calculation of areas; definition of functions (e.g., logarithm, error, and gamma functions); examples of separable differential equations of the form f(y) y

' (t) = g(t)
Taylor series: definition, examples, and convergence
assessment_rules: The final grade for the normal evaluation period is calculated as 30% from each MAP45 and 40% from the final exam. A resit exam of 2 hours will be available, and its grade will be the final grade for the resit period. The final course grade will be the higher of the normal period grade and the resit period grade. On the resit exam date, students may alternatively retake one of the following: 1st MAP45, 2nd MAP45, or the 1st exam, with the higher score being retained for that component. Final grades above 17 must be defended in an oral examination.
